card.name: Commas in encyclopedia-style prose
card.fires_on: The comma after a place name or a completed clause in encyclopedia-style text. It is strongest in biographies after a birthplace and before a state or country, or before a joining word such as but, and, or because.

modes.label: After place names
modes.description: Comma after a city or town in a biography, before the state or country.
modes.example: Karl KautskyArticle Free Pass Karl Kautsky, (born October 16, 1854, Prague<<,>> Bohemia [now Czech Republic]—

modes.label: After a full clause
modes.description: Comma ending a clause in explanatory prose, before a joining word.
modes.example: The market price of common stock is often subject to wide fluctuations<<,>> because it depends largely upon investors’ expectations

card.writes: It suppresses Chinese connecting words and some code-like tokens, so it adds no clear English continuation.
card.plain: It marks a comma in encyclopedia-style writing, often after a place name or at the end of a clause.
